title: Interpolation and algebraic-SLP lower bounds for the EC discrete-log map (Theorems A, A')
question: Theorem A: Let E/F_p (short Weierstrass), P of order r with r != p, 2 <= N <= r-1. If a rational function f on E satisfies f(kP) = k mod p for 1 <= k <= N, then f has pole order (divisor degree) >= (N-1)/2; if f is a polynomial in X, Y then its total degree is >= (N-1)/6. Proof: h(Q) = f(Q+P) - f(Q) - 1 vanishes at kP, 1<=k<=N-1; h != 0 since otherwise iterating r times gives r = 0 in F_p; pole order of h <= 2 * pole order of f. Theorem A': any straight-line program over F_q using +, -, *, / on the coordinates of Q and constants that computes k mod p for all Q = kP, 1<=k<=N, has length >= log2((N-1)/12); charging >= c log q bit operations per field operation gives Omega(n^2) bit cost in this algebraic model (no comparisons/bit extraction).
rationale: Registered by PI from round-5 runs after PI reproduction of numerics.

notes: Agent proof attempt; PI checked the core of A (translation argument). Likely overlaps Lange–Winterhof / Satoh (statements not retrieved): novelty NOT claimed. Toy check: minimal pole order exactly r on 40 curves. A' is a restricted-model statement only. | ECDLP-17 blind review: the stated bounds are TRUE, but the stated PROOF has a gap: "h ≡ 0 ⇒ r = 0 in F_p" fails when p | r with r != p (example p=5, r=10, verified by PI). A' constant log2((N-1)/12) is valid but not sharp ((N-1)/6), and its model (defined divisions, no comparisons) must be explicit; Ω(n^2) only under a per-operation charge. Status "refuted" refers to the proof as stated; the corrected statement and proof are HYP-adb581ff.
